ambiguous_terms.review_note: Blind spot, blind spots and blind area are one concept. AB2001 and AB2687 are linked from "look over your shoulder" and do not use the words blind spot. Confirm those two links before import.

AB2528 states the parking rule, including where one line is broken. AB2007 and BB1236 use "double white lines" for the path past hatch markings and for where you return after overtaking. Those two questions are no longer linked. Confirm that split before import.
ambiguous_terms.previous_explanation_en: Pairs of white lines along the centre of the road. They may both be solid, or one may be broken. You must not park or stop on a road marked with them except to pick up or set down passengers.

ambiguous_terms.review_note: BB1207 answers 50 mph for a car towing a trailer on a single carriageway that "has this sign". The sign is not named in the text, so 50 mph is not stated on this card. Confirm the sign before adding that figure.
ambiguous_terms.previous_explanation_en: The default maximum speed where no lower limit is signed. The actual number depends on the type of road and vehicle. The sign is a white circle with a black diagonal bar.

ambiguous_terms.review_note: Both official cases are now in the explanation: the works-vehicle sign, and a queue moving faster than the lane on your right. Confirm that no other case has been added before import.
ambiguous_terms.previous_explanation_en: To pass on the left side of another vehicle. In the official question, a slow works vehicle shows a sign telling you to pass on its left. Follow the sign and pass with care.

ambiguous_terms.review_note: The bank describes the signal and does not use the name "police stop signal". Confirm the label before import.
The bank describes the colour but does not name a separate stud type. Confirm the label before import.

BB1577 names yellow zigzag lines. AB2545 and AB2729 are picture questions about markings outside schools and do not use the words zigzag lines, so they are not linked. A reviewer who can see the image should confirm whether they belong on this card.

This is medical shock. It is kept separate from the electric shock given by a defibrillator. The aliases are full phrases so the defibrillator questions are not linked. "Frightening event" was removed because the questions do not use it.
ambiguous_terms.previous_explanation_en: A medical reaction after injury or a frightening event. Warning signs include a rapid pulse, sweating, pale skin, and rapid shallow breathing. Keep the person warm and comfortable, do not give them anything to eat or drink, reassure them, and try not to leave them alone.

evidence.snippet: Look over your shoulder for a final check
…ind or to the side of your vehicle. Before you move off, you'll need to look over your shoulder to check for anything not visible in the mirrors.

sample.explanation_en: The area around your vehicle that the mirrors do not show. Look around, including over your shoulder, before you move off, change lane or turn.
sample.example_en: Before you move off from behind a parked car, check the mirrors and look around for the blind spots.
sample.image_concept: A car with shaded zones that the interior and door mirrors do not cover.

sample.explanation_en: A yellow criss-cross box at a junction, painted so the junction does not become blocked. Do not enter unless your exit is clear. You may wait in the box to turn right if your exit is clear but oncoming traffic, or other vehicles waiting to turn right, stops you turning.
sample.example_en: The exit road is full, so you wait before the yellow box instead of driving into it.
sample.image_concept: A yellow box junction, with a car waiting inside only because it is turning right and its exit is clear.

sample.explanation_en: The surfaced strip along the left edge of a motorway. Use it for an emergency or a breakdown, not for a rest or a phone call. On some motorways it can be opened as a running lane when a mandatory speed limit is displayed above it. A red cross above it means it is not open as a running lane.
sample.example_en: If you break down, you may use the hard shoulder. Do not use it for a rest or a phone call.
sample.image_concept: A motorway hard shoulder beside a solid white line, with a gantry that can show either a red cross or a mandatory speed limit above it.

sample.explanation_en: Let other road users go first. Do not make them slow down or stop for you.
sample.example_en: At a pelican crossing, flashing amber means give way to people already on the crossing.
sample.image_concept: An inverted triangular give-way sign and the double broken line at a junction.

sample.explanation_en: A crossing where pedestrians and cyclists may cross at the same time. Cyclists may approach the crossing quickly.
sample.image_concept: A toucan crossing with a pedestrian and a cyclist crossing side by side.

sample.explanation_en: A Statutory Off-Road Notification to the DVLA. It tells them a vehicle is not being used on the public road, so it can stay untaxed. It lasts until the vehicle is taxed, sold or scrapped.
sample.example_en: The car is kept off the road and is not taxed. You make a SORN, and it ends when you tax, sell or scrap the car.

sample.explanation_en: When a tyre rides up on a layer of water and loses contact with the road. The steering can suddenly feel light. Ease off and do not brake until the steering feels normal again.
sample.example_en: In heavy rain the steering suddenly feels very light. That is aquaplaning.
sample.image_concept: A tyre lifted off the road surface on a film of water.

sample.explanation_en: A way to check the gap in front in good, dry conditions. When the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point, you should be able to say "Only a fool breaks the two-second rule" before you reach it. Leave a longer gap in the wet or on ice.
sample.example_en: The car ahead passes a bridge. You should not reach that bridge for about two seconds.
sample.image_concept: Two cars and a roadside post, with a two-second gap marked between them.

sample.explanation_en: Motorway studs between the hard shoulder and the left edge of the carriageway.
sample.image_concept: Red studs between the hard shoulder and the left-hand lane.

sample.explanation_en: A temporary layout, often at roadworks, where traffic is directed onto the opposite carriageway and passes oncoming vehicles without the usual barrier.
sample.example_en: In a contraflow, keep your distance and do not change lanes.
sample.image_concept: A motorway contraflow with cones and traffic passing in both directions on one carriageway.

sample.explanation_en: A pedestrian crossing with sensors that hold the red light while people are still crossing. After green, the next light is steady amber, not flashing amber.
sample.image_concept: A puffin crossing with a sensor watching the crossing area.

sample.explanation_en: The downward force of the trailer hitch on the tow ball. The maximum your vehicle may take is in the handbook. The hitch should press down on the ball, not lift it.
sample.image_concept: A trailer hitch pressing down on a tow ball, labelled as noseweight.

sample.explanation_en: A position for an unconscious person who is breathing, used to help keep the airway open. Keep checking the airway until medical help arrives.
sample.image_concept: A person placed in the recovery position, with the airway kept open.

sample.explanation_en: The default maximum speed where no lower limit is signed. The number depends on the road and the vehicle. For cars and motorcycles, the questions give 70 mph on a motorway or dual carriageway and 60 mph on a single carriageway, unless signs show otherwise. Towing a trailer is lower: the questions give 60 mph on a dual carriageway or motorway. The sign is a white circle with a black diagonal bar.
sample.example_en: The national speed limit applies and traffic is coming towards you, so you use dipped headlights rather than main beam.
sample.image_concept: The national speed limit sign: a white circle with a black diagonal stripe.

sample.explanation_en: White zigzag markings on the approach to, and the exit from, a pedestrian crossing. You must not park on them. The official questions call that illegal and an offence. You must also not overtake the leading vehicle when approaching the crossing. Parking there blocks the view for people crossing and for approaching drivers.
sample.image_concept: White zigzag lines on both approaches to a pedestrian crossing, with a car wrongly parked on them.

sample.explanation_en: An extra lane on a steep uphill stretch for slow vehicles, so faster traffic can pass. Also called a climbing lane.
sample.image_concept: A steep motorway hill with an extra left lane for slow lorries.

sample.explanation_en: Very bright lights at the back for when visibility is seriously reduced. The questions describe this as about 100 metres (328 feet) or less. Switch them off when visibility improves, because they dazzle drivers behind you.
sample.image_concept: A rear fog light switched on in thick fog, and switched off once the road is clearer.

sample.explanation_en: A place where a railway crosses the road. A steady amber light comes on first, then flashing red lights, and you must stop. If you break down on the crossing, get everyone clear and use the railway telephone.
sample.example_en: The amber light comes on as you approach. Stop before the barrier unless you have already crossed the line.
sample.image_concept: A level crossing with amber then flashing red lights and a barrier.

sample.explanation_en: A road where traffic in opposite directions is separated by a central reservation. Each side may have more than one lane.
sample.example_en: Before you turn right onto a dual carriageway, check that the central reservation can shelter your vehicle.
sample.image_concept: A dual carriageway with a central reservation and two lanes each way.

sample.explanation_en: A cane carried by a person who is blind. A white stick with a red band means the person is deaf as well as blind, so they may not hear a horn.
sample.image_concept: A white stick, and a white stick with a red reflective band.

sample.explanation_en: On an automatic, pressing the accelerator firmly through so the gearbox changes to a lower gear and the car can accelerate more quickly.
sample.example_en: You need to accelerate quickly, so you use kick-down rather than changing gear by hand.
sample.image_concept: An accelerator pedal pressed fully down, with the automatic gearbox changing down.

sample.explanation_en: Diagonal stripes painted on the road to separate traffic streams that could endanger each other. If a solid white line borders the area, do not enter it except in an emergency.
sample.image_concept: A hatched area in the centre of the road bordered by a solid white line.

import_later: Import only from Admin → Keyword Cards, after a human reviews this file. The importer writes status = draft and question links only. It requires an explicit confirmation, does not run on page load, and has no bulk-publish action. Do not call the status route. Arabic stays empty until the translation phase. Upload at most one image, and only after the card is accepted.
